sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Neenah, Wisconsin, on your own timeline?
sections.html:
Neenah homeowners can list with an agent, sell privately, or sell to a cash buyer that purchases the house as-is. A listing suits a move-in-ready house with time to spare, while a direct sale suits a house that needs work, an estate, or a firm closing date.

The Census Bureau estimated 27,638 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.1 percent from the 2020 estimates base. About 66.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied home was valued at $210,700 for 2020 to 2024, and median household income was $75,374.

sections.h2: Where is Neenah and what is its history?
sections.html:
Neenah is a city in Winnebago County on the banks of Lake Winnebago, Little Lake Butte des Morts and the Fox River. It lies about 10 miles northeast of Oshkosh and 40 miles southwest of Green Bay, and it is the southwesternmost of the Fox Cities. It shares Doty Island with its twin city Menasha.

Governor James Duane Doty named the place from the Ho-Chunk word for water or running water, and a Ho-Chunk village stood here until 1830. Kimberly-Clark was formed in Neenah in 1872, and it opened a paper mill the next year. Population rose from 1,296 in 1860 to 27,319 in 2020. The city covers just 9.37 square miles of land, which works out to 2,915 people per square mile. The Bergstrom-Mahler Museum, founded in 1959, holds more than 5,000 pieces of glass art, mostly paperweights, Germanic drinking vessels and contemporary studio glass.

sections.h2: What jobs, roads and schools shape the Neenah market?
sections.html:
Paper and steel remain part of the economy, with companies such as Essity and Kimberly-Clark operating here. Plexus, J.J. Keller and Associates, Miron Construction, Menasha Corporation and Theda Clark Hospital are among the companies headquartered in Neenah. Workers spend a mean 18.1 minutes getting to work, shorter than in the other three cities in this guide.

Interstate 41 runs south to north along the city's west side, Valley Transit provides bus service, and Appleton International Airport handles commercial flights. The Canadian National line from Chicago to International Falls passes through.

The Neenah Joint School District lists one high school, one middle school and several elementary options. Those include Alliance Charter School and Clayton, Coolidge, Horace Mann, Lakeview, Spring Road, Taft and Tullar elementary schools, plus the Washington School of Early Learning. The district publishes a boundary map for grades K to 4, so you can confirm which elementary school covers a particular address.

sections.h2: How does the Neenah assessor treat a home you plan to sell?
sections.html:
The City of Neenah's Assessment office is in the Division of Community Development at 211 Walnut St., Room 313, and takes appointments at 920-886-6115 or assessors@neenahwi.gov. Staff handle non-waterfront residential property. A statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc. handles residential waterfront and commercial property, and that contact is Mark Brown at 920-749-1995.

Appraisers visit properties to verify records, carry city photo identification and drive a city vehicle. If a letter from the office arrives while you are preparing to list, schedule the visit, because a corrected record on bedrooms, finished space or additions leaves fewer surprises in a buyer's due diligence. The assessor's page also links the Department of Revenue guide for property owners.

sections.h2: Do Neenah rules cover short-term rentals and home occupations?
sections.html:
The city's planning forms page lists a Tourist House Permit for short-term rentals, along with a home occupation application and a driveway standards sheet. If the house you are selling has been rented to guests, contact Community Development about the permit status before you advertise it as a rental, and ask whether the permit can move to a new owner.

The same page links the city's zoning application used for site plan review, rezoning and plats. The city's Inspections division handles building permits, so contact it if a past owner finished work without one.

sections.h2: Which Wisconsin sale rules apply to a Neenah house?
sections.html:
The real estate condition report is required by Wis. Stat. 709.02 for sales of one-to-four unit properties. The report is due within 10 days after the contract is accepted, and the buyer may rescind within two business days after that window if it is missing. An owner must answer or supply information for every item for the report to count as complete.

The transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 under Wis. Stat. 77.22. At the Census median value of $210,700, the fee would be $632.10. The seller as grantor owes it, and the register collects it with the deed.

  • Deeds in lieu of foreclosure and transfers by will or survivorship are exempt from the fee.
  • Family exemptions in section 77.25 cover transfers for nominal or no consideration, such as parent to child, so an ordinary sale to a relative is still taxed.
  • When the fee does not apply, the reason must be stated on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Winnebago County?
sections.html:
The Winnebago County Register of Deeds explains on its Instruments of Conveyance page what a deed needs. It must name the grantor and grantee, carry a notarized grantor signature and a legal description, show a return address, and place the parcel identification number from the tax bill under that address. Only original deeds with original signatures can be recorded, and photocopies are not accepted.

The recording fee is $30. A Wisconsin transfer return receipt must accompany the deed, and the transfer fee, if any, and the recording fee must come with it. Call the office at 920-232-3394 with questions. Staff offer general guidance but cannot answer legal questions or tell you how to fill out the transfer return, so an attorney or title company should draft the deed.

sections.h2: When are Neenah property taxes due, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
The state's Guide for Property Owners says assessments reflect market value as of January 1 and that bills go out by the third Monday in December. The first installment is due January 31 and the second July 31. Interest on unpaid tax runs at 1 percent per month back to February 1.

Ask the City of Neenah or Winnebago County treasurer for the current-year bill and any special assessments. Your closing agent then splits the tax between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale beat listing in Neenah?
sections.html:
A cash sale trades some price for speed and certainty. You skip open houses, buyer loan approvals and repair negotiations, and the date of closing depends on title work. Listing opens the house to the widest set of buyers, and Neenah's lake and river settings draw interest from buyers who use mortgages.

  • Get the offer in writing, with the closing date and the party who pays title costs.
  • Subtract your payoff, unpaid taxes and any liens to see your net.
  • Compare that net with what listing would likely leave after repairs and time on the market.

faqs.a: Winnebago County does. Its Register of Deeds charges a flat $30 recording fee and requires an electronic transfer return receipt with each deed.

faqs.q: Who handles assessments for Neenah waterfront homes?
faqs.a: A statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc. handles residential waterfront and commercial property. Non-waterfront residential property is handled by City of Neenah assessment staff at 920-886-6115.

faqs.q: Does Neenah have a permit for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's planning forms page lists a Tourist House Permit for short-term rentals. Ask Community Development whether your property has one before you sell.

The Neenah Joint School District serves the city, with Neenah High School, Neenah Middle School and several elementary schools. Its K to 4 boundary map shows which elementary school covers an address.

faqs.q: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Neenah sale?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller. A sale at $210,700, the Census median home value, would owe $632.10 unless an exemption applies.
